comment: Agent Kit registry. Cosmetic only - no keys, no marks. Every theme is a curated variant of the approved Mission Control v2 shell: lesson reading surfaces are never touched, contrast stays AA on the dark shell, and no theme may use background-attachment:fixed or per-card backdrop-filter (Chrome compositor rule). vars map to the THEME KNOB custom properties in style.css :root; stars feeds the starfield canvas; fx names an optional ambient effect layer (comets | aurora).
clearanceNote: Thresholds re-tiered 2 Aug 2026 (DFM 131): every lesson-end must unlock something new in the Agent Kit, so levels 2-6 sit a small margin below the NO-STRETCH full-completion cumulative XP for J1 L1-L5, computed from the built content and the engine award sites (ladder 7+clean*5; vault 12+right*3; casework 4+closed*4+gold+rc*2+ship*3; studio build crits*4+ship*3; gallery 3*given+v2; plus the server's +10 for filing the exit report). Best-path cumulatives: L1 110, L2 148, L3 194, L4 233, L5 275. Levels 2-5 carry two themes each and level 6 carries Gold Command, so the five levels above the start are exactly five unlock moments for five lessons. DAMIEN'S RULINGS, 9 Aug 2026 (DFM 164a then 165): the whole ladder is now tuned to the FLOOR path - the pupil who uses the priced features exactly as designed, buying every Debug Hint, taking every clue, and getting nothing right first try in the Vault. Her cumulatives, computed from the same built content: L1 92, L2 124, L3 164, L4 199, L5 241. Thresholds sit a small margin below each (90, 120, 160, 195, 235), so SHE unlocks something at every lesson-end - the promise rule 131 actually makes. The no-stretch full-completion pupil (110, 148, 194, 233, 275) also crosses exactly one level per lesson. KNOWN AND ACCEPTED, because no ladder can avoid it: a pupil who does EVERY stretch challenge (110, 153, 204, 246, 291) crosses two levels at the end of Lesson 3 and none at the end of Lesson 5, because she is further ahead after three lessons than the floor pupil is after four - the ranges overlap and no single threshold exists. Fixing that properly needs a SEVENTH tier (two more themes), which is new content and his call. Lowering thresholds can only ever GRANT an unlock, never revoke one, so no pupil loses a costume she already had; the mx 'once earned always hers' machinery (DFM 145) is untouched. qa-predeploy pins all three pupil paths and both invariants, so any content edit that shifts these numbers fails loudly.

kitsNote: EVERY WORD ON THE SHARED KIT SURFACES LIVES HERE (his K1 ruling, extended 16 Aug). The kit modal, the level-up pop and both toasts are ONE set of screens serving three years, and J1's agent fiction is J1's alone (DFM 25: a word she must decode before she can reach the content is a cost, not fun). So the rank word, the pop title, the pop body, both toasts and the footer are registry text, not literals in app.js - which also ends the DFM 162b class, where a sentence split across two JavaScript strings renders perfectly and greps to nothing. J1's values reproduce its approved wording character for character (DFM 87/81), proved by a rendered comparison in qa-j1-unchanged.js, never by reading the source. TOKENS: {level} is the level number, {short} the XP still to go.

j1.name: Agent Kit
j1.explainer: Your Agent Kit is kind of like this website’s own wardrobe or costumes!
j1.popBody: It holds the looks and badge designs your console can wear, unlocked as your XP grows. This clearance has just unlocked new ones. Open it to try them on — you can change your look any time from your name chip, top right.
j1.savedToast: Equipped — saved to your Agent File.
j1.lockedToast: Locked — Clearance {level} kit. {short} XP to go, Agent.
j1.foot: Click to equip — every choice saves to your Agent File by itself. Earn XP by completing missions and nailing your checks; higher clearance unlocks more kit.
j1.insigniaLockedToast: That insignia is above your clearance.

j2.name: The Kit Locker
j2.explainer: The Kit Locker is your own locker in the Workshop. Finish lessons and you earn new looks for your screen. They hang in here, and they are yours to keep.
j2.popBody: It holds the looks your screen can wear, and you unlock more as your XP grows. This level has just unlocked new ones. Open the locker to try them on. You can change your look any time from your name chip, top right.
j2.savedToast: Equipped — saved to your Kit Locker.
j2.lockedToast: Locked — this look needs Level {level}. {short} XP to go.
j2.foot: Click to equip. Every choice saves by itself. You earn XP by finishing lessons and getting your checks right, and a higher level unlocks more looks.
j2.insigniaLockedToast: That symbol is above your level.

j3.name: Wardrobe
j3.explainer: Every real studio has a Wardrobe department. This is yours. The looks you have earned live here, and anything you unlock stays yours.
j3.popBody: It holds the looks your screen can wear, and more unlock as your XP grows. This level has just unlocked new ones. Open Wardrobe to try them on. You can change your look any time from your name chip, top right.
j3.lockedToast: Locked — this look needs Level {level}. {short} XP to go.
j3.foot: Click to equip. Every choice saves by itself. You earn XP by finishing lessons and getting your checks right, and a higher level unlocks more looks.
j3.insigniaLockedToast: That symbol is above your level.

worldNote: PER-YEAR DEFAULT WORLDS (his DFM 224b ask - "Each Year group must have it's own distinctive background colour. A soft animation would be great as well" - ruled to these two worlds as K11a, 15 Aug 2026). Each year has a level-1 BASE LOOK, which is an ordinary theme in this registry: j1 midnight (untouched), j2 workbench "The Workbench" (forge charcoal and copper, embers drifting up), j3 screeningroom "The Screening Room" (plum velvet and marquee gold, one beam sweeping). A pupil record stores '' for "the default", and app.js resolves '' through App.defaultThemeId, so the SAME stored value opens three different worlds. midnight is re-tagged j1 (it was "all"), which also kills the stray "classic HQ interface" line from a J2 or J3 wardrobe - the exact agent word DFM 223b removed from the side quest. J1 IS UNCHANGED BY CONSTRUCTION AND BY PROOF: midnight overrides no custom properties and its starfield equals the shell's STAR_DEFAULTS value for value, so resolving to it paints the same screen the stylesheet always painted - asserted in rendered pixels by qa-j1-unchanged.js, not claimed. Palettes and their computed contrast are binding from J2J3_DESIGN_ROUND_PROPOSALS.md section A; the authority at build is qa-readability on rendered pixels, never these numbers. The two fx layers (embers, spotlight) animate transform and opacity only - the Chrome compositor rule that keeps old C2k machines from going black.
yearNote: PER-YEAR REGISTRY (his K1 ruling, 14 Aug 2026: the J2 and J3 rewards must be different from J1’s, in what they are and what they are called). clearancesByYear holds one rank ladder per year; every theme and insignia carries a year tag, and a look may be equipped only when its tag is "all" or matches the class’s year - enforced on the server as well as the client, so a DevTools call cannot cross years. J2 and J3 ship with level 1 ONLY: their level-2 threshold is computed from that year’s BUILT Lesson 1 floor path (DFM 165 - never from memory), so it does not exist until that lesson does, and the kit modal therefore promises nothing it cannot keep (rule 35).
